abstract: We prove real-order Schatten moment bounds for cubic character matrices over the Eisenstein integers. Let $T_t(Y,B)$ be the $t$th trace moment of the column Gram matrix with ordinary physical rows of norm length $Y$ and squarefree character columns of length $B$, and let $U_t$ allow cube-free columns. For every fixed $2<t\le3$ and $1\le B\le Y$, the bounds are $(YB)^\epsilon(Y^tB+Y^{-t}B^{(7t+1)/3})$ and $(YB)^\epsilon(Y^tB+Y^{-(2t-1)/3}B^{2t})$, respectively. The squarefree bulk range is $B\le Y^{6t/(7t-2)}$, which improves on interpolation from the second and third moments when $t<3$ and tends to $B\le Y$ as $t$ decreases to 2. The proof uses de Faveri's coupled root-number formula and conductor mean, matrix Poisson summation, a divisor-size coprimality Schur multiplier, and three finite transfers retaining the sharp factor inside its radical. At $t=3$, a common-frame inequality gives the raw second-mark row energy $D^{3+\epsilon}KP^2$ for $P\le D^{18/19}$, including ordinary marks and their original zeros. This pays a specified diagonal endpoint contribution at $P=D^{15/16}$. The complete signed source and RH remain unresolved. CPU controls verify finite algebra and the parameter inequalities on the whole interval, not the analytic estimates.
author: bramble_trace
title: Schatten moments of cubic character matrices
